findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Fix the claim --review 'gate applies?' check to mirror plan_review_precheck's full exemption logic (gate_enabled check + ticket-type exemption), not just claim_gate_check, so exempt ticket types receive the 'plan-review gate not enabled for this ticket; --review skipped' notice and do not trigger an unnecessary LLM review.
evidence: Plan: 'when --review is set and the gate applies, call llm.claim_gate_check(ticket_id); if it reports not-ok, run review_plan(sign=True)'
Plan: 'prints a one-line notice "plan-review gate not enabled for this ticket; --review skipped" and the claim proceeds — never a silent no-op'
gates.py:170: 'if ticket_type in ("bug", "session_log", "code_review", "identity"): return None  # exempt from the plan-review gate'
attest_gate.py:99-151: claim_gate_check — no ticket-type check anywhere in function body; returns ok=False for missing attestation regardless of ticket type
findings.finding: The claim --review logic uses claim_gate_check as the sensor for 'does the gate apply?', but claim_gate_check checks attestation validity only — it does not check ticket-type exemption (bug/session_log/code_review/identity). plan_review_precheck (the authoritative gate) exempts those types before calling claim_gate_check. As a result, for a bug ticket where the gate is enabled but no attestation exists, claim_gate_check returns ok=False, --review triggers review_plan (unnecessary LLM work), and the specified 'plan-review gate not enabled for this ticket; --review skipped' notice is never printed. The plan's stated condition 'when the gate applies' is inconsistently implemented between the mechanism description and the existing exemption logic.
findings.location: Approach section — claim --review mechanism; gates.py:160-171 (plan_review_precheck exemption); attest_gate.py:99 (claim_gate_check, no ticket-type check)
scenarios: User runs `rebar claim BUG-123 --review` when require_plan_review_for_claim is enabled. claim_gate_check returns ok=False (no attestation). review_plan is invoked, runs a light advisory review (always PASS for bugs), burns LLM tokens. The 'skipped' notice is never emitted. The claim then proceeds through plan_review_precheck which exempts the bug type anyway.
If --review is supposed to be a cheap 'only review if needed' convenience, running the full LLM review on a bug that will be exempted by the gate contradicts that intent.
findings.suggested_fix: In the claim --review implementation, first call gate_enabled(..., 'require_plan_review_for_claim', ...) and check ticket_type against the exempt set (matching plan_review_precheck's logic at gates.py:160-171) before falling through to claim_gate_check. Only invoke review_plan when the gate is enabled AND the ticket type is not exempt AND claim_gate_check reports not-ok.

findings.finding: For `edit --review`, the plan specifies only the exit-code mapping on non-PASS outcomes; it does not specify that the review's finding summary (or any human-readable output) is printed to the user. In contrast, `claim --review` explicitly states 'the command prints the review's finding summary'. This asymmetry means a user whose edit was committed but whose review returned BLOCK would receive a non-zero exit code with no console explanation, while a claim user would receive the summary.
findings.location: Approach section — edit --review subsection; compare with claim --review: 'the command prints the review's finding summary and exits with the disposition mapping'
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the edit --review approach: 'on a non-PASS verdict, print the review's finding summary before exiting' and add a unit-test assertion that the printed output contains the verdict reason for BLOCK and INDETERMINATE stubs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the 'finding summary' output for `claim --review` non-PASS paths: name whether `_render_plan_review_text` is reused or define which verdict-dict fields (e.g., `blocking[]`, `indeterminate[]`, `coverage.resolution_class`) are printed and in what format.

plan_review_verdict.schema.json defines blocking[], advisory[], indeterminate[], coaching[] etc. — multiple candidate fields, no selection rule specified
ABSENCE: no AC line specifies which fields are rendered or asserts the rendering matches any particular output format

findings.location: Approach section, claim --review paragraph: 'the command prints the review's finding summary and exits with the disposition mapping'
scenarios: Implementer invents a minimal one-line print (e.g., only the verdict string) that satisfies no practical user need on a BLOCK
Implementer duplicates _render_plan_review_text logic with subtle divergence, creating two code paths for the same output
A test asserts specific output text that the implementer's chosen format does not produce, causing a false test failure
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, replace 'prints the review's finding summary' with 'calls `_render_plan_review_text(result)` (the same helper used by `rebar review-plan`)' and add a corresponding AC assertion: 'claim --review BLOCK output includes at least one [BLOCK ...] line per blocking finding (checked: unit test asserting output contains the finding text from the stubbed verdict)'.

findings.finding: The plan says claim --review on BLOCK/INDETERMINATE/retryable-degrade 'prints the review's finding summary' but never defines which verdict-dict fields constitute that summary or names the rendering function to use. The codebase already has _render_plan_review_text (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:583) that reads blocking[], advisory[], indeterminate[], coaching[], coverage.counts, etc. — but the plan does not reference it. An implementer reading only the plan cannot determine what output to produce for the non-PASS paths.
findings.location: Approach section, claim --review paragraph: 'the command prints the review's finding summary'
findings.suggested_fix: In the Approach, replace 'prints the review's finding summary' with 'renders the result via _render_plan_review_text(result) (the same rendering used by the review-plan CLI) then exits with _disposition_exit_code(result, indeterminate_code=2)'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the user-facing error message for the edit --review exception path, making clear that the edit was committed and instructing the user to run `rebar review-plan <id>` separately rather than retrying edit --review.
evidence: 'both flags let the exception propagate to the standard CLI error handler' — no bespoke user-facing message is specified
The plan specifies help-text warnings about non-atomicity but only for the concurrent-reconvergence case, not for the provider-failure case
findings.finding: After edit --review raises (exception path), the user's edit IS committed but the standard CLI error message does not convey this. The plan specifies no error message content clarifying that the edit succeeded while the review failed, leaving the user uncertain whether to re-run edit --review (which creates a new EDIT event) or run review-plan separately.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Exception path' paragraph; AC: 'A raising review_plan propagates through the standard CLI error path with the edit still committed'
scenarios: User sees a generic error and re-runs edit --review, not knowing the edit already committed
User does not know they can run `review-plan` separately and instead re-edits the ticket unnecessarily
findings.suggested_fix: Add a try/except around the review_plan call in edit --review that catches BaseException, prints 'Edit committed. Review failed: <error>. Run `rebar review-plan <id>` to complete the review.' to stderr, then re-raises (or exits with the standard error code).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Capture the 'embed prerequisite verification in consuming verb' pattern in an ADR or AGENTS.md section (covering: CLI-only scope, no parent-cascade propagation, MCP fence, and the OSS precedent rationale) so future contributors have a persistent, findable decision record.
evidence: Plan Context: 'OSS precedent favors embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb… over new fused commands'
Plan Approach: 'The flag is NOT propagated through the parent-first cascade' and 'Both flags are CLI-only (the MCP surface keeps its REBAR_MCP_ALLOW_LLM fence)'
Scope: no ADR file listed; AGENTS.md not mentioned
findings.finding: The plan establishes a new architectural pattern — embedding prerequisite verification inside consuming verbs rather than requiring a separate fused command — but does not capture this decision in an ADR, AGENTS.md entry, or design-doc update. Future contributors adding flags to other verbs (e.g., `merge --review`, `close --review`) have no persistent record of the precedent, trade-offs, or constraints (e.g., 'flag is CLI-only; not propagated through parent cascade; MCP surface is fenced').
findings.location: Context / Approach sections; no ADR scoped
scenarios: A contributor later adds `rebar merge --review` and, lacking the decision record, propagates it through the parent cascade or exposes it on MCP — violating constraints that exist only in this plan's prose.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify timeout and/or retry/backoff behavior for the LLM call within --review flags, and ensure transient provider exceptions either map to exit code 11 or are documented as unretryable so callers can act accordingly.
evidence: 'if review_plan RAISES (provider outage, config error) instead of returning a verdict dict, both flags let the exception propagate to the standard CLI error handler'
No mention of timeout, retry, backoff, or circuit-breaker for the LLM call itself anywhere in the plan
Exit code 11 ('retryable per ADR 0040') applies only to 'retryable-degrade stubs' returning verdict dicts, not to raised exceptions
findings.finding: The plan specifies no retry, backoff, or timeout for transient LLM provider failures (network timeout, rate-limit, 5xx) under either --review flag. The 'retryable degrade' exit code 11 applies only to verdict dicts returned by review_plan, not to exceptions raised by it. When the provider is slow or throttling, the call blocks indefinitely and then raises, giving no graceful-degradation or circuit-breaker path.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Exception path' paragraph; Testing section — 'a RAISING review stub'
scenarios: Provider is rate-limiting: call hangs for minutes then raises; user cannot distinguish transient from permanent failure
Provider is intermittently flaky: retrying manually re-runs edit --review, appending a new EDIT event each time

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add at least a structured log entry (e.g., WARNING level with ticket_id, flag, and exception class) for each review_plan failure under --review, so operators can observe and alert on the new failure points.
evidence: ABSENCE: no mention of logging, metrics, or tracing for review_plan calls or their failure outcomes under the new flags
'both flags let the exception propagate to the standard CLI error handler' — no structured log before re-raise is mentioned
findings.finding: The plan introduces new LLM call failure points under --review for both edit and claim, but specifies no observability instrumentation (structured log entry, metric counter, or trace span) for these paths, making it impossible for operators to distinguish provider outages from user errors or to alert on elevated --review failure rates.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Exception path' paragraph; Scope section
scenarios: Production spike of LLM provider errors under --review goes undetected until users complain
Operator cannot tell from dashboards whether failures are provider outages or misconfigured claim gates

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Acknowledge in the plan whether duplicate EDIT events from retried `edit --review` invocations are acceptable (idempotent by design) or whether a deduplication/guard strategy is needed, and document the decision.
evidence: 'for edit --review the EDIT remains committed (it landed before the review started) and the process exits via the normal error path'
No idempotency guard or deduplication logic for the EDIT event on re-invocation is mentioned
findings.finding: For edit --review, when review_plan raises (provider outage), the EDIT event is already committed to the store. If the user re-invokes `rebar edit <id> ... --review` to retry, a second EDIT event is appended with identical field changes. The plan does not acknowledge this accumulation or provide guidance, making the edit --review invocation non-idempotent on exception-then-retry.
findings.location: Approach section — 'Exception path' paragraph; AC: 'A raising review_plan propagates through the standard CLI error path with the edit still committed'
scenarios: User retries edit --review after a transient provider failure, producing two identical EDIT events in the store
Automation script retries on non-zero exit and accumulates N EDIT events before the provider recovers

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct or replace the terraform prior-art analogy in the Context section: `terraform apply <planfile>` enforces separation of plan from apply (the two-step pattern), not embedding — replace with a more accurate precedent (e.g. `git push --force-with-lease` embeds a safety pre-flight, or `npm publish` runs pre-publish lifecycle hooks) that genuinely supports embedding verification in the consuming verb.
evidence: Plan quote: 'OSS precedent favors embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb (cargo publish verifies by default; terraform apply consumes a staleness-checked plan artifact) over new fused commands.'

terraform apply requires a prior, separate `terraform plan` to produce the plan file; `terraform apply <planfile>` does check staleness but does NOT embed the plan-generation step in the apply verb — it enforces separation, not embedding.

The cargo publish analogy does hold (cargo runs verify steps internally), but terraform is the analogy used to justify consuming a 'staleness-checked plan artifact', which actually maps to the existing two-step `review-plan` + `claim` flow, not to the proposed `claim --review` embedding.
findings.finding: The terraform prior-art analogy used to justify the 'embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb' pattern is inverted: terraform apply does NOT embed the plan step — it consumes a pre-produced plan artifact from a separate `terraform plan` invocation, which is actually the two-step sequence the plan labels 'hazardous'. The cited precedent therefore describes the opposite pattern.
findings.location: Context / Problem — 'OSS precedent favors embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb (cargo publish verifies by default; terraform apply consumes a staleness-checked plan artifact)'
scenarios: A future plan reviewer or architect pushes back on the --review embedding pattern using the terraform counterexample; the cited precedent becomes a liability rather than a defense.
A reader unfamiliar with terraform interprets the analogy as supporting the new pattern and approves based on flawed reasoning.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the terraform clause with: 'git push --force-with-lease embeds an optimistic-concurrency pre-flight in the push verb' or 'npm publish runs prepack/prepublish hooks inline' — both are accurate examples of embedding prerequisite verification in the consuming verb.

findings.finding: The plan specifies _disposition_exit_code mapping for verdict dicts returned by review_plan, but is completely silent on what edit --review and claim --review do when review_plan raises an exception (LLMError on hard context-assembly failure, confirmed in the live docstring). The existing review-plan CLI handles this with an explicit 'except llm.LLMError' at src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:524-526. No AC or test covers this path for the new flags.
findings.location: Approach section (both edit --review and claim --review paragraphs); Testing and Acceptance Criteria sections
findings.suggested_fix: Add to both flag-handler descriptions: 'If review_plan raises LLMError, write the error to stderr and exit 1 (matching the existing _review_plan CLI handler at _llm_commands.py:524-526). Add a unit test stub that raises LLMError and asserts exit 1 and no claim attempted.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `src/rebar/_commands/gates.py` (the recovery message at lines 213-215) to the Scope and update it to reference `claim --review` so the in-code guidance matches the new flag.
